fields.quote: Besides these variants, we further include the best-reported results from original papers in the literature for comparison (denoted as SOTA).
fields.reason: SOTA and many BART cells are best-reported numbers from prior papers (table superscripts), while Flan-T5 and T0 appear without source citations in the same harness. That is neither a full re-run nor unreported.

fields.quote: We utilize the large versions of T5.1.1 and ExT5, and all the results of them are from Aribandi et al. (2022).
fields.reason: T5.1.1/ExT5 scores are explicitly taken from Aribandi et al., and SOTA/BART cells cite original papers, but Flan-T5 and T0 numbers have no such attribution, so copying is only partial.

claims.quote: For the second stage that integrates single-task pre-trained prompts (denoted as MVP+S), we compare it with two variants using different prompts
claims.reason: Authors claim task-specific prefix-prompt pre-training as their method. MVP+S vs MVP+R (same backbone and layer-wise prompts, prompts randomly initialized without pre-training) and vs MVP+M is a matched with/without comparison, with results in Table 2, so ablation is YES not merely a confounded table.

claims.quote: supervised pre-training models (i.e., MVP, Flan-T5, and Single) achieve better performance than the unsupervised pre-trained model BART
claims.reason: They state supervised pre-training for NLG as their own gap-filling TRAIN contribution. The MVP/Single vs BART contrast exists at the same 406M size, but MVP is BART further trained on extra labeled data, so data and tokens are not matched: PARTIAL.
